Sourdough bread at home

Sourdough baking at home starts with a lively starter, good flour and patience. This guide walks through feeding schedules, hydration, shaping and scoring so your loaf rises tall and bakes with a crisp, blistered crust and an open, glossy crumb every single time you try. Feeding your starter

Hydration

Keep the starter at one hundred percent hydration, feed it twice a day with equal weights of flour and water, and use it when it has doubled and smells pleasantly sour rather than sharp.
